summary: T-0621 [file-robustness, substrate, changes_product=0]: PgFileStore's DAO ops (insertFile/insertVersion/setCurrentVersion/getFile/getVersion/maxVersionNo) historically ran on their OWN autocommitting pool connection, NOT on the withTenantTx client the upload route (POST /api/records/:recordId/files) opens around insertFile+addVersion — T-0620's pr-handoff named this residual gap explicitly ('withTenantTx is cosmetic for PgFileStore'). A genuine mid-transaction DB error (not a PDP deny — T-0620 already closed that case) thrown inside addVersion AFTER insertFile had already committed independently could not be rolled back by the outer tx, leaving an orphan choros.file row (current_version=NULL, zero versions). Fix: every PgFileStore method gains an OPTIONAL trailing `executor?: Queryable` parameter (mirrors T-0636's PostgresJobStore.enqueue(executor?) precedent exactly), defaulting to this.pool (zero behaviour change for every omitting caller). New `PgFileStore.boundTo(executor): FileMetaSource` returns a view whose every method delegates to `this.<method>(...,executor)` — this is the seam that lets addVersion (pure-core, FF-PURE, must not import pg) transparently run its DAO calls on a caller-supplied connection without ever knowing pg.PoolClient exists. The upload route now passes the withTenantTx client as insertFile's executor and as boundTo's argument for addVersion's meta dependency — insertFile + every DAO call addVersion makes now run on ONE Postgres transaction; a throw anywhere rolls back the entire sequence, no orphan possible from a DB-level failure.
test_proof_of_fix: ci/checks/db/file-store-tx-atomicity.db.test.ts (NEW, 4 tests, live Postgres): FF-621-ATOMIC-FAIL — a PgFileStore subclass whose insertVersion always throws (simulating a genuine mid-transaction DB error AFTER insertFile ran in the SAME withTenantTx callback), wired into the real HTTP route, causes the upload to fail (>=500) AND leaves choros.file row count UNCHANGED for the record — proving the tx rolled back insertFile too (before T-0621 this would have left an orphan current_version=NULL row, since insertFile committed independently on its own connection the instant it ran). FF-621-ATOMIC-OK — regression guard: a normal successful upload still commits file+version together (201, current_version points at the new version, exactly 1 version row). FF-621-TENANT — the bound tx executor inherits the SAME SET LOCAL choros.tenant_id GUC withTenantTx already set: a file inserted for tenant A is invisible when read scoped to tenant B, visible scoped to its own tenant. FF-621-BOUNDTO-UNIT — direct unit-level proof PgFileStore.boundTo(client) actually threads the executor: insertFile+insertVersion+setCurrentVersion via the bound view are visible to a read via the SAME bound view on the SAME uncommitted transaction (read-your-writes), then ROLLBACK, then a separate PgFileStore instance confirms the row does not exist post-rollback.
ci/checks/db/file-write-authz.db.test.ts (T-0620, PRE-EXISTING, unmodified, re-run green 7/7) — proves this task does not regress the PDP-deny orphan-fix or authz-parity behaviour T-0620 established.

live_proof_plan: Substrate task (changes_product=0) — no product-visible behaviour changes, so no founder-facing LIVE_PROOF is applicable per D-064's own carve-out for substrate/infra tasks. The proof is the db-test suite above: a real Postgres mid-transaction failure (not a mock) is exercised through the real HTTP route with the real Router/withTenantTx/PgFileStore wiring, only the innermost insertVersion call is fault-injected via subclassing — everything else (BEGIN/SET LOCAL/insertFile/ROLLBACK) is the genuine production code path.
tx_threading_approach: PgFileStore gains a `Queryable` interface (structurally identical to pgJobStore.ts's own Queryable: {query<T>(text, values?): Promise<{rows:T[]}>}, satisfied by both pg.Pool and pg.PoolClient — the exact T-0636 P0-6 precedent, PostgresJobStore.enqueue(...,executor?: Queryable)). Every DAO method gains an optional trailing `executor?: Queryable` param, resolving `const q = executor ?? this.pool` before querying. New `PgFileStore.boundTo(executor): FileMetaSource` returns a view delegating every FileMetaSource method to `this.<method>(...,executor)` — this is how addVersion (pure-core, cannot import pg — FF-PURE) gets tx-awareness without any change to core/file-attachment.ts or the FileMetaSource interface it exports. files.ts's upload route: `withTenantTx(pool, tenantId, async (client) => { await fileStore.insertFile(file, client); const vResult = await addVersion({..., meta: fileStore.boundTo(client), ...}, ...); return vResult; })` — client was previously unused (`_client`) and is now the explicit executor threaded through both insertFile and addVersion's internal DAO calls (getFile/maxVersionNo/insertVersion/setCurrentVersion, all reached via the bound view).
fix: 1) src/core/postgres/pgFileStore.ts: new `Queryable` interface + `executor?: Queryable` optional trailing param on insertFile/getFile/getVersion/maxVersionNo/insertVersion/setCurrentVersion/markContentErased/updateRetentionState (each resolves `const q = executor ?? this.pool`); new `boundTo(executor): FileMetaSource` method. 2) src/http/files.ts: withTenantTx callback parameter renamed `_client`→`client` (now used); `fileStore.insertFile(file, client)` and `addVersion({..., meta: fileStore.boundTo(client), ...})` replace the prior `fileStore.insertFile(file)` and `meta: metaStore`; doc comments updated to describe the new atomic behaviour and mark the old per-connection framing as historical/fixed. 3) src/__tests__/files-http.test.ts: FakeFileStore gains `boundTo(executor): FileMetaSource { return this; }` (additive fixture fix, required because the fake is cast to PgFileStore and the route now calls boundTo on it).
